input.requirement_description: After content goes live, we need to track how it performs and pay creators accordingly. Creators get a base fee plus bonus based on performance. Brands want to see campaign analytics — how much reach, engagement, ROI. Payments should be batched weekly. We have an existing payment service.
input.context: The system is a FastAPI microservice called campaign-service. We have existing User, Content, Payment, and Notification services. Tech stack: Python, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery. Campaigns, applications, content submissions, and review workflows already exist. Each accepted creator has a negotiated base_fee stored on the application record. Content has a published_at timestamp and a post_url linking to the live note on XHS.

structured_spec.overview: After a creator's content is published on XHS, the platform tracks its performance over a 7-day observation window, calculates final payment (base fee + performance bonus), batches payments into a weekly settlement cycle, and surfaces analytics dashboards for both brands and creators.

user_stories.story: As the system, I want to automatically begin tracking performance metrics when a creator confirms their content is published, so that settlement can be calculated based on real data.
acceptance_criteria: When a content submission enters 'published' status (creator provides post_url and confirms), a performance tracking record is created with status 'tracking'
The tracking window is 7 calendar days from published_at (inclusive of publication day)
A periodic Celery task (every 4 hours) syncs metrics from the Content Service for all actively tracked posts: views, likes, comments, shares, link_clicks
Each sync creates a timestamped metric snapshot; the latest snapshot is treated as the authoritative metric set
After the 7-day window closes, the tracking record transitions to 'pending_calculation'

user_stories.story: As the system, I want to calculate final payment amounts when the tracking window closes, so that creators are paid accurately.
acceptance_criteria: A Celery task runs daily, selects all tracking records in 'pending_calculation' status, and computes payment for each
Payment = base_fee (from application) + performance_bonus

Performance bonus is computed from campaign-level bonus rules: a list of (metric_name, threshold, bonus_amount) tuples. If the creator's metric meets or exceeds the threshold, the corresponding bonus_amount is added. Multiple bonuses can stack.
All monetary calculations use Python Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP and 2 decimal places
A PaymentRecord is created with: creator_id, campaign_id, application_id, base_fee, bonus_breakdown (JSON list of applied bonuses), total_amount, status='calculated'
The tracking record transitions to 'calculated'
If a PaymentRecord already exists for the same application_id, skip (idempotency guard)

user_stories.story: As the system, I want to batch-process calculated payments weekly so that creators receive timely payouts.
acceptance_criteria: A Celery beat task runs every Monday at 02:00 UTC
It selects all PaymentRecords with status='calculated' created before the current batch cutoff (Sunday 23:59 UTC)
For each record, it calls the Payment Service's transfer API with: creator_id, amount, idempotency_key (derived from payment_record_id)
On success: PaymentRecord status → 'settled', settlement_batch_id recorded, settled_at timestamp set
On failure: PaymentRecord status → 'settlement_failed', error_message recorded, record remains eligible for the next batch retry
A settlement batch summary record is created: batch_id, total_records, total_amount, success_count, failure_count, batch_started_at, batch_completed_at

user_stories.story: As a content creator, I want to view my earnings for each campaign so that I understand how I was paid.
acceptance_criteria: Creator can list their payment records with pagination, filtered by campaign_id or status
Each record shows: campaign title, base_fee, bonus_breakdown (which bonuses triggered and why), total_amount, status, settled_at
Creator can view a summary: total_earned, total_pending, total_campaigns_participated
Returns 403 if the requesting user is not the payment record's creator

user_stories.story: As a brand marketing manager, I want to view campaign analytics so that I can measure ROI and compare creator performance.
acceptance_criteria: Brand can view per-campaign analytics: total_reach (sum of views), total_engagement (sum of likes + comments + shares), total_clicks, total_spend, average_cost_per_engagement, ROI_ratio (total_engagement / total_spend)
Brand can view per-creator breakdown within a campaign: creator name, post metrics, payment amount, cost_per_engagement
Brand can view an aggregate dashboard across all campaigns: total_spend, total_reach, average_engagement_rate, top-performing campaigns
Analytics data is served from pre-aggregated materialized views or cache, not computed on-the-fly
Returns 403 if the requesting user is not the campaign owner

user_stories.story: As a content creator, I want to see my performance metrics for published content so that I can track how my content is doing before settlement.
acceptance_criteria: Creator can view the current metric snapshot for each of their published content pieces
Shows: views, likes, comments, shares, clicks, last_synced_at, days_remaining in tracking window
Shows estimated bonus (based on current metrics vs. campaign bonus thresholds) clearly labeled as 'estimated — final amount calculated after tracking window closes'
Returns 403 if the requesting user is not the content's creator

user_stories.story: As a platform admin, I want to view settlement batch history and retry failed payments so that I can ensure all creators are paid.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can list settlement batches with: batch_id, date, total_records, total_amount, success/failure counts
Admin can view failed payment records within a batch with error details
Admin can trigger a manual retry for individual failed payment records or an entire failed batch
Admin can view a system-wide settlement health dashboard: total_unsettled, oldest_unsettled_days, failure_rate_trend
Returns 403 if user is not an admin

tracking_transitions.trigger: campaign cancelled or content deleted during tracking window

payment_transitions.trigger: admin retries or next weekly batch
dispute resolved in favor of original amount
dispute resolved with adjustment, difference refunded to brand

edge_cases.scenario: Creator deletes their published post during the 7-day tracking window
edge_cases.handling: Tracking record transitions to 'cancelled'. Creator forfeits performance bonus but still receives base_fee. A PaymentRecord is created with bonus_amount=0. Notify brand that content was removed.

edge_cases.scenario: Performance data sync fails for multiple consecutive cycles (Content Service downtime)
edge_cases.handling: Metric sync task logs warning and retries with exponential backoff (4h → 8h → 16h). If no successful sync occurs within the 7-day window, use the last available snapshot. If zero snapshots exist, flag for manual admin review and hold settlement. Do NOT auto-calculate with zero metrics.

edge_cases.scenario: Settlement batch job crashes mid-processing — some payments transferred, others not
edge_cases.handling: Each payment transfer uses an idempotency_key derived from payment_record_id. On restart, the batch resumes from where it left off. Already-settled records are skipped (idempotent). Batch summary reflects actual outcomes.

edge_cases.scenario: Creator's performance metric exactly equals the bonus threshold (e.g., threshold is 10,000 views, creator gets exactly 10,000)
edge_cases.handling: Bonus IS awarded — threshold comparison uses >= (greater than or equal to). This must be explicitly documented in the bonus rules and consistently applied.

edge_cases.scenario: Campaign is cancelled by brand after content is published but before the tracking window closes
edge_cases.handling: Tracking continues for already-published content. Creator receives base_fee + any earned bonus as if the campaign completed normally. Brand is still charged. Rationale: creator fulfilled their obligation.

edge_cases.scenario: Metric data is corrected by Content Service after settlement was already calculated (e.g., bot traffic removed, view count adjusted downward)
edge_cases.handling: If PaymentRecord status is 'calculated' (not yet settled): recalculate and update. If status is 'settled' or later: do NOT auto-adjust. Flag for admin review and potential manual dispute resolution. Never claw back from creator automatically.

edge_cases.scenario: Partial payment failure in a batch — Payment Service returns insufficient_balance for the platform wallet
edge_cases.handling: Stop processing remaining records in the batch. Mark all unprocessed records as 'settlement_failed' with reason='platform_balance_insufficient'. Alert platform admin immediately. Already-settled records in this batch are NOT rolled back.

edge_cases.scenario: Brand's campaign had total_spend > total_engagement_value — negative ROI
edge_cases.handling: Display negative ROI honestly in analytics. Do not hide or mask it. Show it as a red metric with context: 'Campaign spend exceeded estimated engagement value.' Do not affect settlement — creators are still paid regardless of brand ROI.

edge_cases.scenario: Two tracking windows for the same creator on the same campaign (creator had revision → resubmit → re-publish)
edge_cases.handling: Only the latest published version is tracked. Previous tracking records for superseded content versions are cancelled. Payment is calculated based on the final published content only.

edge_cases.scenario: Floating-point arithmetic produces a payment of 99.999999999 instead of 100.00
edge_cases.handling: All monetary calculations MUST use Python Decimal type with explicit ROUND_HALF_UP rounding to 2 decimal places. Never use float for monetary values. This is enforced by code review and a linting rule on the PaymentRecord model.

clarifying_questions.question: What is the exact bonus formula? Is it a fixed amount per threshold, a percentage of base_fee, or a tiered/progressive structure?
clarifying_questions.impact: A tiered structure (e.g., 10K views = +200 CNY, 50K views = +800 CNY, 100K views = +2000 CNY) behaves very differently from a per-unit structure (e.g., +0.01 CNY per view above 10K). Affects calculation complexity and payment predictability.
clarifying_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Fixed amount per threshold (simplest). Campaign defines a list of {metric, threshold, bonus_amount} rules. Each rule is independently evaluated.

clarifying_questions.question: Is there a cap on total bonus per creator, or can a viral post earn unlimited bonus?
clarifying_questions.impact: Uncapped bonus could exceed campaign budget. Capped bonus is safer but may feel unfair to high-performing creators.
clarifying_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Total payment (base + bonus) is capped at the campaign's max_fee. This protects budget while allowing bonus earning.

clarifying_questions.question: How should tax withholding be handled? Does the platform deduct individual income tax before paying out, or is the creator responsible?
clarifying_questions.impact: If platform withholds tax, we need tax rate configuration, tax certificate generation, and a more complex settlement pipeline. If creator is responsible, the payout is gross amount.
clarifying_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Platform pays gross amount to creator. Tax is the creator's responsibility. (Simplification for v1, but flag for legal review.)

clarifying_questions.question: What is the dispute resolution process if a creator disagrees with their payment amount?
clarifying_questions.impact: Requires dispute state in payment lifecycle, admin tools for investigation, potential manual payment adjustment.
clarifying_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Creators can raise a dispute within 30 days of settlement. Admin reviews and can either confirm or adjust the amount. Adjustments create a supplementary payment record.

clarifying_questions.question: Should the 7-day tracking window be configurable per campaign, or is it a platform-wide constant?
clarifying_questions.impact: Configurable windows add flexibility (brand can set 3-day or 14-day tracking) but complicate batch scheduling and comparability of analytics across campaigns.
clarifying_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Platform-wide constant of 7 days for v1. Make it a configuration constant (not hardcoded) so it can be changed or made per-campaign later.

clarifying_questions.question: What is the refund policy if a brand wants money back for underperforming content?
clarifying_questions.impact: If brands can request refunds, we need a refund workflow, budget reconciliation, and creator notification. This significantly increases complexity.
clarifying_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No refunds for v1. The brand accepted the creator and approved the content — payment is guaranteed once content is published. Analytics help brands make better decisions on future campaigns.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All monetary calculations MUST use Python Decimal type with ROUND_HALF_UP rounding to 2 decimal places. Float types are prohibited in any model, schema, or function that handles money.
non_functional_requirements.rationale: Floating-point arithmetic errors (e.g., 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004) are unacceptable for financial calculations. Even 0.01 CNY discrepancy at scale becomes a reconciliation nightmare.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Payment calculation and settlement transfer operations must be idempotent. Repeated execution with the same input must produce the same result without side effects (no duplicate payments).
non_functional_requirements.rationale: Celery tasks can be retried on failure. Settlement batch jobs can crash and restart. Without idempotency, creators could be paid twice — a critical financial risk.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: PaymentRecord creation must be transactional with tracking record status update. If payment record creation fails, tracking status must not advance to 'calculated'.
non_functional_requirements.rationale: Inconsistent state (tracking says 'calculated' but no PaymentRecord exists) would cause the settlement batch to miss the payment.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Campaign analytics dashboard queries must respond within 500ms (p95) for campaigns with up to 500 creators and 7 days of metric history.
non_functional_requirements.rationale: Analytics is a frequently accessed page by brand managers. Slow dashboards lead to user frustration and repeated page refreshes that compound load.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Settlement batch jobs must emit structured logs with: batch_id, records_processed, records_succeeded, records_failed, total_amount_settled, duration_ms. Failed records must include error_code and error_message.
non_functional_requirements.rationale: Financial operations require auditable trails. When a payment fails, the on-call engineer needs to diagnose and retry within the same business day.
